page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on KVM hypervisor technology. Hardware specifications include 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. The system carries 64.0 GB of memory, allocating 4.0 GB per vCPU, backed by 33 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. This instance has no bundled local storage and includes no GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight a distinction between single-threaded efficiency and parallel scaling. Single-core processing measures in the lower quartile, reflected by a stress-ng single-core result of 1106.79 and a Geekbench single-core score of 949.0. Sequential operations like gzip compression (19.02 GB/sec) and bzip3 single-threaded decompression (7.48 GB/sec) also display lower performance tiers. Conversely, multi-core and application metrics fall squarely within average benchmark tiers. Multi-core stress-ng achieves 11738.07, PassMark CPU score reaches 12950.69, static web serving throughput measures 7.75 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations execute at 11.72 million operations per second. Small LLM model (135M) prompt processing maintains average throughput at 815.98 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.g5ne.4xlarge lies in its reliance on multi-threaded execution to offset modest single-core throughput. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance provides a stable resource footprint for general computing without overprovisioning memory. Because local ephemeral storage is absent, all persistent storage requirements depend entirely on attached network volumes. Qualitatively, the instance offers balanced resource efficiency for parallelized enterprise workloads, web application servers, Redis caching nodes, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
